x: Commentary on Sūrat “Alam nashraḥ”. In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
On the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h

Did We not expand for you your breast (1) And remove from you your burden (2) Which weighed upon your back (3) And raise high for you your repute (4) For indeed, with hardship comes ease (5) Indeed, with hardship comes ease (6) So when you have finished, then toil (7) And to your Lord direct your longing (8)

. The Exalted, whose mention is lofty, says to His Prophet Muḥammad, reminding him of His favours upon him and His kindness to him, and urging him thereby to give thanks for what He has bestowed upon him so that he may merit increase from Him:
h
Did We not expand for you
, Muḥammad, for guidance, faith in God and knowledge of the truth,
h
your breast
, so that We softened your heart for you and made it a vessel for wisdom?
h
And remove from you your burden
. He says: and We forgave you your past sins, and lifted from you the weight of the days of pre-Islamic ignorance in which you had been.
In the reading of ʿAbdallāh, as it is reported
n
: “and We loosened from you your load.”
h
Which weighed upon your back

. He says: which burdened your back and weakened it. This is from their saying of a camel that has returned from a journey, which the journey has weakened and whose flesh it has taken away: “he is the wreckage of a journey.”
The people of interpretation have said the like of what we have said about this.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us; and al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Warqāʾ told us,
m: both of them from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid on the saying of God:
And remove from you your burden

evidence.text: In the reading of ʿAbdallāh, as it is reported (1): “and We loosened from you your load.”

x: And His saying:
h
Which weighed upon your back
. He said: weighed heavily upon your back.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatādah,
m: Did We not expand for you your breast (1) And remove from you your burden (2) Which weighed upon your back
: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had sins that had burdened him, and God forgave them for him.

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatādah,
m: . He said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had sins that had burdened him, and God forgave them for him

c: I was told on the authority of al-Ḥusayn,
m: he said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd told us, he said: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say, on His saying:
And remove from you your burden
: he means the polytheism he had been in

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, on His saying:
Did We not expand for you your breast (1) And remove from you your burden
. He said: He expanded his breast for him and forgave him his sin that he had before he was made a prophet, and so removed it. And on His saying:
. He said: it burdened him and exhausted him, as a heavy load wears down a camel until it becomes wreckage after having been fat.
And remove from you your burden
: it burdened your back; We removed it
from you and lightened for you what had burdened your back.

x: And His saying:
h
And raise high for you your repute

. He says: and We raised your remembrance high for you, so that I am not mentioned except that you are mentioned with Me. That is their saying: “There is no god but God; Muḥammad is the Messenger of God.”
The people of interpretation have said the like of what we have said about this.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Abū Kurayb and ʿAmr b. Mālik told us, both said: Sufyān b. ʿUyaynah told us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid:
m: And raise high for you your repute
. He said: I am not mentioned except that you are mentioned with Me: “I bear witness that there is no god but God, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is the Messenger of God”

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatādah,
m: And raise high for you your repute

. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Begin with servanthood and follow with messengership.” I said to Maʿmar [what that means]. He said: [It is] “I bear witness that there is no god but God and that Muḥammad is His servant”—that is servanthood—and His messenger is that you say: “His servant and His messenger”

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatādah:
m: And raise high for you your repute

: God raised his remembrance in this world and the next, so there is no preacher, nor one reciting the testimony, nor one at prayer, except that it is proclaimed with it: “I bear witness that there is no god but God, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is the Messenger of God”

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: ʿAmr b. al-Ḥārith informed us, from Darrāj, from Abū l-Haytham, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, from the Messenger of God,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “Gabriel came to me and said: ‘My Lord and your Lord says: How have I raised your remembrance high for you?’” He said: “God knows best.” [Gabriel] said: “When I am mentioned, you are mentioned with Me”

x: And His saying:
h
For indeed, with hardship comes ease (5) Indeed, with hardship comes ease

. The Exalted, whose mention is lofty, says to His Prophet Muḥammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Indeed, with the hardship you are in—from striving against these polytheists, and from the beginning of what you are undertaking—there is hope and relief, in that He will give you victory over them, until they submit to the truth you have brought them, willingly or unwillingly. It is reported from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that when this verse was revealed he gave his Companions the good news of it, and said
n
: “One hardship will never overcome two eases.”
Mention of the report to that effect:

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: al-Muʿtamir b. Sulaymān told us, he said:
m: I heard Yūnus say: al-Ḥasan said: When this verse was revealed:
, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Rejoice! Ease has come to you; one hardship will never overcome two eases”

c: Yaʿqūb told me, he said: Ibn ʿUlayyah told us, from Yūnus, from al-Ḥasan the like of it, from the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace

c: Muḥammad b. al-Muthannā told us, he said: Muḥammad b. Jaʿfar told us, he said: ʿAwf told us, from al-Ḥasan, from the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, to the like of it.

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from al-Ḥasan, he said:
m: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out one day delighted and joyful, laughing, and he was saying: “One hardship will never overcome two eases, one hardship will never overcome two eases;
For indeed, with hardship comes ease (5) Indeed, with hardship comes ease

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatādah,
m: For indeed, with hardship comes ease
: It was mentioned to us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave his Companions the good news of this verse, and said: “One hardship will never overcome two eases”

c: Ibn al-Muthannā told us, he said: Muḥammad b. Jaʿfar told us, he said:
m: told us, from Muʿāwiyah b. Qurrah Abū Iyās, from a man, from ʿAbdallāh b. Masʿūd, he said: If hardship were to enter a hole, ease would come until it entered upon it; for God says:
For indeed, with hardship comes ease (5) Indeed, with hardship comes ease

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Wakīʿ told us, he said: Shuʿbah told us, from a man, from ʿAbdallāh,
Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us; and al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Warqāʾ told us,
m: both of them from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, on His saying:

x: And His saying:
h
So when you have finished, then toil
The people of interpretation differed concerning the interpretation of this.
Some of them said: Its meaning is: when you have finished your prayer, then toil toward your Lord in supplication, and ask Him for your needs.
Mention of those who said that:

c: ʿAlī told me, he said: Abū Ṣāliḥ told us, he said: Muʿāwiyah told me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās,
m: So when you have finished, then toil

c: Muḥammad b. Saʿd told me, he said: my father told me, he said: my uncle told me, he said: my father told me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās:
m: So when you have finished, then toil
. He says: when you have finished what was made obligatory upon you of prayer, then ask God, direct your longing to Him, and toil for Him

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us; and al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Warqāʾ told us,
m: both of them from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, on His saying:
So when you have finished, then toil
. He said: when you stand for prayer, then toil in your need toward your Lord

c: I was told on the authority of al-Ḥusayn,
m: he said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd told us, he said: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say, on His saying:
So when you have finished, then toil
. He says: from the obligatory prayer, before you give the salām, then toil

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatādah,
m: So when you have finished, then toil (7) And to your Lord direct your longing
. He said: He commanded him, when he had finished his prayer, to be earnest in his supplication.

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatādah,

x: Others said: Rather, its meaning is:
h
So when you have finished
striving against your enemy,
h
then toil
in worship of your Lord.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatādah, he said:
m: So when you have finished, then toil
. He said: He commanded him, when he had finished his campaigning, to strive in supplication and worship

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, on His saying:
So when you have finished, then toil
. He said, from his father: when you have finished the striving—the striving against the Arabs—and their resistance has ceased, then toil in the worship of God,
And to your Lord direct your longing

x: Others said: Rather, its meaning is: when you have finished the affairs of your worldly life, then toil in the worship of your Lord.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid:
m: So when you have finished, then toil
. He said: when you have finished the affairs of the world,

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Wakīʿ told us, from Sufyān, from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid:
m: So when you have finished, then toil
. He said: when you have finished the affairs of your worldly life,

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Jarīr told us, from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid,
m: . He said: when you have finished the affairs of the world and have stood for prayer, then make your longing and your intention for Him

. The most correct of the views on this is the view of those who said: God, whose mention is lofty, commanded His Prophet to make his leisure from everything he was occupied with—of the affairs of his worldly life and his afterlife, whatever the occupation with it had burdened

him with and whatever he had been commanded to be occupied with—into toil in His worship, occupation with what brings him near to Him, and asking Him for his needs. He did not specify any one state of his leisure to the exclusion of another; all states of his leisure are alike, whether his leisure was from prayer, or striving, or a worldly affair with which he had been occupied, because of the generality of the condition in that, with no specification of one state of leisure to the exclusion of another.

x: And His saying:
h
And to your Lord direct your longing

. The Exalted, whose mention is lofty, says: and to your Lord, Muḥammad, direct your longing, to the exclusion of all others of His creation, since these polytheists of your people have directed their longing, in their needs, to the gods and the rivals.
The people of interpretation have said the like of what we have said about this.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid:
m: And to your Lord direct your longing
. He said: make your intention and your longing toward God

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Wakīʿ told us, from Sufyān, from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid:
m: And to your Lord direct your longing
. He said: make your longing and your intention toward your Lord (1).

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us; and al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Warqāʾ told us,
m: both of them from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, on His saying:
And to your Lord direct your longing
. He said: when you stand for prayer
. End of the commentary on Sūrat “Alam nashraḥ”.

notes.en: Al-Farraʾ mentioned this reading in Maʿani al-Qurʾan (3/275); it is anomalous because it conflicts with the written form of the codex.

Ibn Hibban (no. 3382) transmitted it through Ibn Wahb, and Abu Yaʿla (no. 1380) through Darraj. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/364) to Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu Nuʿaym in al-Dalaʾil.

Al-Bayhaqi transmitted it through the same chain in al-Shuʿab (no. 10011). ʿAbd al-Razzaq transmitted it in his Tafsir (2/380–381) through Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi from Ibn Masʿud. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/364) to Saʿid ibn Mansur, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, and Ibn al-Mundhir.
